source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Health benefits: research has shown that corn is not merely a filling starchy food -- it also contains many nutrients beneficial to the body.

Antioxidant compounds: corn contains phytonutrients and carotenoids as its main antioxidants (especially in yellow corn), including lutein, zeaxanthin, vanillic acid, ferulic acid, and other antioxidant compounds.

Carbohydrates: corn provides carbohydrates as an energy source the body needs daily for physical activity and exercise, particularly beneficial for athletes.

Protein: corn kernels contain a moderate amount of protein, which is a nutrient the body needs for tissue growth and repair.

Substances that do not cause excessive weight gain: corn contains nutrients useful for health, and importantly contains substances that do not cause significant fat/weight gain.

Fiber: corn contains dietary fiber beneficial for health, similar in some ways to the fiber found in bran and beans, and beneficial for the digestive system.

Food uses: corn serves as a daily staple food for people in the Americas and Africa; it is used as a supplementary/complementary food; and it is used as feed for livestock.

Raw material uses: corn is also processed into paper, alcohol/liquor, cosmetics, corn oil, soap, ink, and glue/adhesive for the paper-manufacturing industry.
